sources.fullCitation: Photograph of Franz Waxman rehearsing with Les Brown for the 1955 Los Angeles Music Festival, credited "Photo: Dave Pell." Musical Courier, vol. 152, no. 1 (July 1955), p. 27. Summy-Birchard Publishing Company. Scanned copy openly viewable at the Internet Archive. The issue copyright was not renewed: the Online Books Page inventory of periodical renewals records the first renewed issue of the title as May 1961. Accessed 6 August 2026.

media.altText: Detail of a 1955 magazine photograph showing Franz Waxman in glasses, playing a saxophone.
media.description: The printed caption identifies the two men by what they are holding rather than by position: "FRANZ WAXMAN (with saxophone), music director and conductor of the 1955 Los Angeles Music Festival, rehearses with Les Brown for the opening night concert of the Festival on June 6. Waxman conducted Brown's Band of Renown and the Festival Symphony Orchestra in the West Coast premiere of Liebermann's Concerto for Jazz Band and Symphony Orchestra." The archive reproduces the man with the saxophone. The photograph carries the credit "Photo: Dave Pell."
media.publicCaption: Franz Waxman, who appears in this archive with Trouble for Two (1936), A Day at the Races (1937) and The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn (1939). The photograph is much later: he was rehearsing with Les Brown's Band of Renown for the opening concert of the Los Angeles Music Festival in June 1955, which he conducted.
media.publicCreditLine: Photograph credited to Dave Pell; Musical Courier, vol. 152, no. 1 (July 1955), p. 27; Summy-Birchard Publishing Company; scanned copy at the Internet Archive.
media.rightsNote: Public domain in the United States. The photograph was published in Musical Courier in July 1955, inside the 1931–1963 window in which copyright had to be renewed after twenty-eight years. The inventory of periodical renewals compiled by the Online Books Page from the Catalog of Copyright Entries and the Copyright Office records shows the first renewed issue of the title as May 1961, so the issue copyright for 1955 was not renewed and lapsed on 1 January 1984. The same inventory notes that individual contributions to the title were sometimes renewed separately; a photograph carrying only a caption credit is unlikely to have been registered as one, but the possibility is recorded here rather than passed over. The archive holds a 340 × 491 px detail cropped to Waxman.
